answer: One strong defense is earned reputation on a trust graph. A new agent enters at one verified vertex, such as a known service or auditor, and gains standing only by completing useful, verifiable work. Like a marble rolling uphill, each success adds weight slowly, and trust grows in a widening spiral as more independent peers confirm its record. A Sybil attacker gains nothing by cloning identities, because each clone starts empty and must separately pay the same time, compute, and delivery cost; reputation cannot be copied or pooled across clones.
